answers.U1-S1: A man remembers a walk to a river when he was six, where he first saw flamingos, and nothing he saw later was ever as amazing.
answers.U1-S2: He was young and scared of the cattle, but he really wanted to be with his brother, so he went anyway once he was promised safety.
answers.U1-S3: To show how long and hard the walk was for a small six-year-old boy, having to go around plants and push through tall grass.
answers.U1-S4: slowly and seriously, in a calm, dignified way
answers.U1-S5: Because when the wings opened they showed a beautiful bright crimson color he hadn't seen before, which made the bird look even more amazing.
answers.U1-S6: That the birds were rare there; the brothers had never come that far to the river before, so it was new to all of them.
answers.U1-S7: Because it was so beautiful and graceful, white and rose with glowing crimson wings spread out, it seemed heavenly to him.
answers.U1-S8: Later he only saw them in big flocks from far away on a high bank, not close up like the three birds at the river, so it felt less special.
answers.U1-S9: It jumps ahead to his later life and shows that even after seeing flamingos many times, the first sighting stayed the best.
answers.U1-S10: Fond and nostalgic; he still treasures the memory and feels it was special.
